name.text: Diagonals and projections in a cuboid

questiontext.text:
{@ctx@} is a cuboid ABCDEFGH with AB = {@ll@}, BC = {@ww@} and AE = {@hh@} {@un@}.

[[jsxgraph width="360px" height="280px"]] (function() { var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-1.2, 6.2, 8.9, -1.6], axis: false, grid: false, keepaspectratio: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}}); // oblique projection: receding edges at 30 degrees, half length function P(x, y, z) { return [x + 0.5*y*Math.cos(Math.PI/6), z + 0.5*y*Math.sin(Math.PI/6)]; } var solid = {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}; var hid = {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}; var dot = {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}; var tx = {fixed: true, highlight: false, useMathJax: false, fontSize: 15, anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'middle'}; var cx = 3.87, cy = 2.0; function lab(Q, s) { var dx = Q[0]-cx, dy = Q[1]-cy, r = Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy) || 1; b.create('text', [Q[0]+0.42*dx/r, Q[1]+0.42*dy/r, s], tx); } function seg(Q, R, o) { b.create('segment', [Q, R], o); } function mark(Q, R, S) { // right-angle mark at Q between QR and QS function u(X) { var dx = X[0]-Q[0], dy = X[1]-Q[1], r = Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy); return [0.3*dx/r, 0.3*dy/r]; } var a = u(R), c = u(S); b.create('polygon', [[Q[0]+a[0], Q[1]+a[1]], [Q[0]+a[0]+c[0], Q[1]+a[1]+c[1]], [Q[0]+c[0], Q[1]+c[1]]], {fixed: true, highlight: false, fillOpacity: 0, vertices: {visible: false}, borders: {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}}); } // cuboid ABCDEFGH: l = 6, w = 4, h = 3 (shape only) var A = P(0,0,0), B = P(6,0,0), C = P(6,4,0), D = P(0,4,0), E = P(0,0,3), F = P(6,0,3), G = P(6,4,3), H = P(0,4,3); seg(A,B,solid); seg(B,C,solid); seg(B,F,solid); seg(C,G,solid); seg(A,E,solid); seg(E,F,solid); seg(F,G,solid); seg(G,H,solid); seg(H,E,solid); // hidden corner D: its three edges dashed seg(A,D,hid); seg(D,C,hid); seg(D,H,hid); lab(A,'A'); lab(B,'B'); lab(C,'C'); lab(D,'D'); lab(E,'E'); lab(F,'F'); lab(G,'G'); lab(H,'H'); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

The diagram is not drawn to scale.

(a) Find the length of the projection of AG on the plane {@pl@}.

[[input:ans1]] {@un@} [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Find the length of AG.

[[input:ans2]] {@un@} [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

Give lengths correct to 2 decimal places and angles correct to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the final answer.

generalfeedback.text:
(a) Drop a perpendicular from the cuboid to the plane {@pl@}: {@foot@}, so the projection of AG is {@prj@}, a diagonal of a face with sides {@ca@} and {@cb@} {@un@}: \({@prj@}^2 = {@ca@}^2 + {@cb@}^2 = {@S1@}\), so {@prj@} = {@d2(t1)@} {@un@}.

(b) Triangle AG{@prj@} has a right angle where the perpendicular {@thd@} meets the plane: \(\mathrm{AG}^2 = {@S1@} + {@third@}^2 = {@S2@}\), so AG = {@d2(t2)@} {@un@}. Keep \({@prj@}^2 = {@S1@}\) rather than the rounded length.

questiondescription.text:
Three-Dimensional Geometry: length of a projection and a space diagonal

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.4: Find the length of the projection of the space diagonal of a cuboid on a face, then the space diagonal, by Pythagoras twice.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 34, Section B, the worked example and question B3 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Higher 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: new contexts and dimensions, the projection on a stated face found first, randomised, with named feedback and follow-through.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: That is {@op1@}, the projection of AG on {@ol1@}. For the plane {@pl@}, drop the perpendicular from the end of AG that is not in {@pl@}: where does it land?
That is {@op2@}, the projection of AG on {@ol2@}. For the plane {@pl@}, drop the perpendicular from the end of AG that is not in {@pl@}: where does it land?
You found \({@prj@}^2 = {@S1@}\) but did not take the square root.
Your answer is close but not accurate to 2 decimal places. Keep full calculator accuracy until the end (store values, or keep the square root), then round the length once.

falsefeedback.text: The projection of AG on {@pl@} is a diagonal of that face, so its square is the sum of the squares of the two edges of the face. Your answer squared is {@d2(sq1)@}. Which two of the edges {@ll@}, {@ww@} and {@hh@} {@un@} lie in {@pl@}?

feedbackvariables.text: ftv: if is(ans1 > 0) then float(sqrt(ans1^2+third^2)) else NC; dq: float(ans2^2-ans1^2);

truefeedback.text: You found \(\mathrm{AG}^2 = {@S2@}\) but did not take the square root.
Adding the three edges gives a path along the edges, not the straight line.
You added {@prj@} and {@thd@}. They are two sides of a right-angled triangle with AG as the hypotenuse: \(\mathrm{AG}^2 = {@prj@}^2 + {@thd@}^2\).
Your method is right: \(\mathrm{AG}^2\) = (your projection)\(^2 + {@third@}^2\). Check part (a).
Your answer is close but not accurate to 2 decimal places. Keep full calculator accuracy until the end (store values, or keep the square root), then round the length once.

falsefeedback.text: AG is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle: its other sides are the projection from (a) and the edge at right angles to {@pl@}. With your two answers, (b)\(^2\) minus (a)\(^2\) is {@d2(dq)@}; it should be the square of that edge. Which of {@ll@}, {@ww@} and {@hh@} {@un@} is at right angles to {@pl@}?
